title: Good and Bad Strategy
coreMove: Replace ambition language with a diagnosis of the governing obstacle and a coordinated set of actions that actually fit it.
sourcePressure: Apple in 1997 shows the difference between strategy and ambition: Jobs narrowed product lines, channels, manufacturing, inventory, and software work around the real obstacle instead of adding slogans or broad effort.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Good strategy means having a bold vision, tighter costs, or more executive energy.

sourceAnchors.name: Apple in September 1997
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar presents Apple as close to bankruptcy before Jobs narrowed product lines, retailers, software efforts, manufacturing, and inventory around survival in personal computers
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Apple was not saved by louder ambition; the visible move was a hard narrowing of products, channels, software, factories, and inventory around the problem in front of it.

sourceAnchors.name: Steve Jobs
sourceAnchors.detail: Jobs returned and cut the desktop models down to one while reducing portable and handheld lines, peripherals, retailers, and operating complexity
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Jobs made the strategy visible by cutting the product maze down until the company could act coherently again.

sourceAnchors.name: Microsoft $150 million investment
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar names Microsoft's $150 million investment as part of Apple's stabilization story
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Microsoft investment mattered because it bought time for a narrower operating logic, not because money alone became the strategy.
